answer: Each new agent must burn real computation to register: a proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty rises with the signup rate, so a gale of fake identities meets a rising wall of cost. An honest agent pays once, then slowly earns a beacon of portable reputation — a public vertex in the trust graph that others can inspect before dealing. A Sybil farmer pays that fee for every throwaway account, each starting with no history, no vouchers and no rewards, so forging a crowd costs more than the fraud could return.
